# Local rank transform: Properties and applications

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patrec.2011.02.005Get rights and content

## Abstract

In this paper we discuss about some interesting properties of local rank transform and also about some possible applications of this transform such as in edge extraction and image enhancement. An interesting convergence property on the iterative application of this transform on a signal has also been proved in this work.

### Research highlights

► The work discusses about definition and properties of Local Rank Transform (LRT). ► It introduces the concept of-LRT and its uses in developing image processing algorithms. ► The work presents new algorithms of edge extraction and color image enhancement based on LRT.

## Introduction

Rank transforms (Conover and Imam, 1981) are often used in statistics in regression analysis and hypothesis testing. In image processing local ranks of pixels have been used in different image operations specially, in filtering impulsive noise (Abreu and Mitra, 1995). Transformation of pixels to their local ranks is referred in this work as Local Rank Transform (LRT). This transform space is not new to the researchers and there are earlier reports on application of these transforms in pattern matching (Banks et al., 1999, Banks et al., 2001, Wang, 2004), and face recognition (Lahdenoja et al., 2006, Smeraldi, 2002). In this work, we would like to elaborate more on the properties of rank transforms or Local Rank Transforms as referred here. We would also demonstrate some possible applications of these transforms in edge extraction and image enhancement. One of the advantage of rank transform is its low computational requirement as the basic operation required for implementing this transform is the comparison operation.

## Rank transform for noisy images

One may observe that the LRT is very much sensitive to presence of noise in the data. That is why one may require to perform smoothing or low-pass filtering operation before applying the transform. Interestingly, one may extend the definition of local rank to make the transform more suitable in a noisy environment.

## Applications

One of the advantage of LRT is its low computational requirement. The transform is carried out in O(n) time and storage complexities. Moreover, as the basic operations are comparisons and counting, the computations are performed using integer arithmetic only. ## Conclusion

In this work, we discuss about some of the properties and applications of the local rank transform (LRT) of signals and images. With the precise mathematical definition of local ranks, we show that the iterative applications of transform leads to the convergence. The definition is further extended for handling noisy data and called in this work as δ-local rank transform (δ-LRT). The δ-LRT is found to be useful in extracting edges and enhancing images.   * ### Combining sparse representation and local rank constraint for single image super resolution

2015, Information Sciences

Citation Excerpt :

Recently, local rank transform, as a useful tool for describing the data distribution characteristics, is usually used in statistical analysis [7], object detection [14], image denoising [1] and stereo matching [2]. In this paper, considering that local rank can extract better edge information and is insensitive to noise than other edge operator [21], we develop the local rank edge constraint and introduce it into the linear combination stage for SISR task. By combining this edge constraint and the sparse representation, we propose a new SISR method, which can better reconstruct HR image with less edge artifacts and sharp edges.

Show abstract

Sparse representation based reconstruction methods are efficient for single image super resolution. They generally consist of the code stage and the linear combination stage. However, the simple linear combination has not considered the image edge constraint information of image, and hence the classical sparse representation based methods reconstruct the image with the unwanted edge artifacts and the unsharp edges. In this paper, considering that the local rank is able to extract better edge information than other edge operator, we propose a new single image super resolution method by combining the sparse representation and the local rank constraint information. In our method, we first learn the local rank of the HR image via the traditional sparse representation model, and then use it as the edge constraint to restrict the image edges during the linear combination stage to reconstruct the HR image. Furthermore, we propose a nonlocal and global optimization model to further improve the HR image quality. Compared with many state-of-art methods, extensive experimental results validate that the proposed method can obtain the less edge artifacts and sharper edges.
